exposure: e-health lifestyle intervention (diet, physical activity, and well-being advice)
outcome: maternal perceived confidence of dietary change
cohort: A cohort of 57 pregnant women (43.9% overweight/obese) recruited at 8-11 weeks gestation, primarily from obstetric private practices.
finding: The e-health intervention was feasible, improved maternal perceived confidence in dietary change and readiness to exercise, and resulted in infants weighing less and having a lower ponderal index at 3 months postpartum in the intervention group, though no difference in gestational weight gain or birth size was detected.
birth_weight: Not explicitly stated; 'birth size' was measured but showed no difference between groups; infants weighed 5405g (intervention) vs 6193g (control) at 3 months.
